ExecutiveSummary.OverallPosture: Passive external reconnaissance of getmarlee.com identified a medium exposure posture across 1 resolvable subdomain(s). The assessment surfaced 1 high-severity and 1 medium-severity indicators warranting structured remediation attention.
ExecutiveSummary.TopRiskOne: Sensitive service ports publicly reachable (21) — direct attack surface for credential brute-force, vulnerability exploitation, and lateral movement.
ExecutiveSummary.TopRiskTwo: HSTS header absent — browsers may permit unencrypted HTTP connections, exposing session tokens to network-level interception.
ExecutiveSummary.RecommendedNextStep: Prioritise remediation of High-severity findings within the next 30 days. Schedule a follow-up passive assessment in 90 days to validate posture improvement.
ExecutiveSummary.PassiveAssessmentStatement: This assessment relied exclusively on passive, publicly observable signals. No intrusive testing, exploitation, or active probing was performed at any stage.

Findings.LikelyThreatScenario: An adversary positioned on the same network segment as a target user (hotel Wi-Fi, conference network) initiates an SSL Strip attack using a tool such as sslstrip. Because HSTS is absent, the victim's browser accepts an unencrypted HTTP connection. The attacker captures the session cookie from the HTTP request and replays it against the application's authenticated API, achieving full account access.
AttackPath: Full Account Takeover — User Data Accessed
Findings.TechStackRemediation: In Cloudflare Dashboard → SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → Enable HSTS with max-age=31536000 and includeSubDomains.
Findings.RemediationRecommendation:
In Cloudflare Dashboard → SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → Enable HSTS with max-age=31536000 and includeSubDomains.

General guidance: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload' to all HTTPS responses. Submit the domain to the HSTS preload list at hstspreload.org once confirmed stable.

Findings.LikelyThreatScenario: The detected framework version is cross-referenced with CVE databases, revealing a known Remote Code Execution vulnerability. The attacker downloads a public proof-of-concept and validates it against the target without triggering any security alerts. A reverse shell is established, granting operating system level access to the application server and all data it can reach.
AttackPath: Attacker Researches Known CVEs for Identified Version
Exploit Code Sourced from Public Repositories
Findings.TechStackRemediation: Apply remediation according to your web server and framework documentation.
Findings.RemediationRecommendation: Suppress version-revealing response headers (Server, X-Powered-By, X-Generator). In Nginx: server_tokens off; In Apache: ServerTokens Prod; ServerSignature Off. Ensure all detected frameworks are on current stable versions.
